authority.source: Actual human maintainer request in the trusted chat, relayed by the root context.
authority.request: After clarification that the site remains eylema.dev, the user confirmed: Siteyi Google ve Bing arama sonuclarindan da kaldir. Existing direct authority covers the coordinated merges and website deployment.
authority.scope: Persistent noindex on the still-accessible website, disabling indexing promotion, plus separately performed Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster reversible URL removal requests. This plan grants no authority itself.
authority.excluded: No DNS mutation, domain move, account deletion, property removal, verification-token removal, paid action, access-policy change or source/runtime deletion.

implementation: Generate exactly one robots meta tag with noindex,follow on both landing pages. Keep 404 noindex. Preserve canonical/hreflang, language routing, social metadata, accessibility and all current content.

Set globalHeaders.X-Robots-Tag to noindex,follow in the Azure configuration, covering HTML and non-HTML resources including images and release/verification documents. Retain existing security/revalidation headers and true 404 routing; prohibit per-route overrides that remove or contradict noindex.
Keep robots.txt as User-agent: * and Allow: /. Do not add Disallow or a robots.txt Noindex rule: crawlers need access to see HTML/HTTP removal directives. Remove Sitemap promotion.
Keep the existing sitemap URL but generate a valid empty sitemap urlset. This retracts old URL promotion without adding a new broken public route. Do not submit it as a new indexing request.

Keep webmaster verification and public IndexNow ownership key bytes unchanged. Preserve historical submission receipts. Disable manual tools/indexnow.py submission before any preflight fetch or POST; --submit must fail clearly and nonzero, while any retained preview is explicitly non-submitting.
Revise repository gates from indexability to the accepted noindex policy. Preserve all existing language, content, generated output, identity, security, release, MIME and negative checks.

Extend live checks to require noindex headers on release.json, every manifested resource, final canonical/normalized routes and the custom404. Continue verifying exact release commit, full source hashes, MIME, true404 and assets without redirects.

Update paired EN/TR discovery/quality documentation and append a current scoped removal record. Distinguish deployed persistent directives, temporary owner-panel requests and observed final indexing status. Never rewrite historical receipts into removal success.
panel_work_owned_by_root: Preserve verified Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster properties, credentials and inspection access.

Request the existing canonical site's full URL prefix/directory removal using the actual UI choices, documenting scope and request status. Cover both language routes and asset URLs when the panel permits prefix scope.
Read back requests; record pending/approved/failed states separately from published noindex and actual index reports. Do not claim permanent removal from temporary acceptance or search-query absence.
No new indexing, sitemap promotion or IndexNow request is included. Root may retract old sitemap promotion in the authorized search-removal scope without removing the properties.

acceptance_mapping.S1_persistent_page_and_resource_policy: Builder/checker tests accept EN/TR noindex,follow and reject restored index meta, duplicate/conflicting bot directives, missing/contradictory global headers and route overrides. Host headers apply to assets as well as pages.
acceptance_mapping.S2_crawler_access: Generated output and negative tests require the reviewed crawl-permitted robots file without Sitemap promotion; empty sitemap parses and contains zero loc entries. Crawl-blocking mutation fails.
acceptance_mapping.S3_no_promotion: Mocked and actual local CLI tests demonstrate IndexNow submission refusal with zero fetch/POST network calls and nonzero CLI exit; verification bytes and historical receipts remain unchanged.
acceptance_mapping.S4_release_and_browser: Run exact repository commands plus build/fingerprint checks. Verify local browser EN/TR access and navigation; full live canonical release verification requires normal HTTPS on eylema.dev, matching commit/assets/MIME and noindex headers.
acceptance_mapping.S5_independent_delivery: Genuine separate reviewer binds final exact head and acceptance evidence. Required current CI, authorized merge and deployment follow existing workflow. Live release/crawl acceptance remains pending if canonical DNS fails.
acceptance_mapping.S6_search_engine_outcome: Root records actual Google/Bing temporary-removal request readback and later authoritative URL/index states. Search engines process asynchronously; directive or request success alone never means final removal.

exact_local_checks: Reviewed English/Turkish fingerprint refresh and filled PR-body validation

budgets.bounded_network_requests: Existing per-fetch25-second and IndexNow30-second bounds are not expanded; disabled submission makes no request. Engine processing is asynchronous and is reported outside implementation time.

Registry does not explicitly list blanket website qualification; no new domain, numerical, inference or training qualification is invented.

roles.root: Performs authorized webmaster UI requests and final delivery; configured gpt-6-astra/ultra reported by root, hidden serving identity unknown.
roles.independent_final_reviewer: Pending separate owner-approved context on final commit; architect is not the final reviewer.

risks_and_limits: Canonical domain DNS is reported failing; read-only diagnosis is permitted, DNS changes are excluded. Crawler inability to fetch means published noindex cannot yet establish removal, even if the Azure generated hostname works.
HTML-only noindex leaves directly indexed images/other assets uncovered; require global HTTP noindex and actual live response checks.
robots crawl blocks prevent engines from observing noindex; prevent contradictory directives with regression checks.
Temporary Search Console/Bing blocks expire and are separate from persistent directives; retain property verification and inspection to track outcome.
Global header coverage is a deployment claim only after observed live responses; local Python http.server does not implement Azure header configuration.
Noindex is search-engine policy, not authentication or secrecy; the user expressly retains the accessible site.
rollback: A future direct maintainer decision can restore indexability through a separately reviewed source/config/documentation change; do not automatically cancel removal requests or resume submissions.
